title.zh: 人體內部的基因拼圖：SMaHT 聯盟如何繪製非癌組織體細胞突變的「終極導航圖」
title.en: The Cellular Mosaic: Mapping the Hidden Mutations of the Human Body Telomere to Telomere

summary.zh:
【總結】我們常以為全身細胞共用同一套完全相同的遺傳密碼，但事實上，每個人都是由攜帶各異突變的細胞交織而成的「嵌合體」（somatic mosaicism）。美國國家衛生研究院主導的 SMaHT 聯盟（人體組織體細胞嵌合體網絡）在頂級期刊《細胞》（Cell）發表了里程碑式的研究，建立了當前全球最完整、最嚴謹的體細胞突變檢測基準。研究團隊藉由產生超過 1,000 倍深度的短讀長與數百倍長讀長測序數據，全面評估了從單鹼基突變到巨型染色體結構變異的偵測能力。這項成果不僅為科學界提供了標準化分析指南，更證明結合「個體特異性基因組組裝」、「雙端分子測序」與「單細胞測序」三維聯防，能將突變目錄拓展至過去被視為測序死角的極端重複序列，為衰老、神經發育及非癌症重大疾病的研究奠定了全新基石。

【研究問題】細胞在每一次分裂與生命暴露中都會不可避免地累積突變。這些後合子突變（post-zygotic mutations）雖然不會遺傳給下一代，卻深刻牽動著自閉症、癲癇等神經發育疾病、心血管病變以及人體衰老進程。然而，要在正常組織中精確捕獲這些突變，就像在喧鬧的萬人體育館中尋找一名特定人士的低聲耳語。正常組織中的突變等位基因頻率（VAF）極低（通常小於 1% 至 5%），在一般 30–50 倍測序深度下極易與儀器噪聲混淆；現有的單細胞全基因組擴增又面臨等位基因丟失與人為擴增偏差；以往癌症領域建立的突變檢測法高度仰賴「腫瘤與正常配對組織對比」，在缺乏對照組的正常組織中完全無用武之地。科學界長年缺乏一套公認的黃金標準數據集與演算法規範。

【研究方法】SMaHT 聯盟設計了四組兼具純度與真實生理複雜度的基準實驗：第一組「HapMap 混合樣本」，將 6 株具近乎完整端粒到端粒（T2T）組裝的細胞株依特定比例混合，模擬 0.25% 至 16.5% 頻率的已知變異；第二組「COLO829 癌細胞與正常細胞混合樣本」，模擬低於 5% 頻率的突變；第三組採集具自然亞純系結構的「皮膚纖維母細胞」與其衍生之 5 株誘導性多能幹細胞（iPSC）；第四組則直接深入真實臨床情境，分析 4 位正常遺體捐贈者的 6 種冷凍組織。研究橫跨 Illumina 短讀長、PacBio HiFi 與 Oxford Nanopore 長讀長等主流技術，系統化評估了 6 種雙端分子測序（duplex sequencing）技術與單細胞初代模板定向擴增（PTA）法，並突破性地將「捐贈者特異性二倍體組裝」（DSA）及泛基因組圖譜引入比對流程，全面取代傳統單一參考基因組（GRCh38）。

【結果】研究確立了多項突變檢測的黃金準則與硬指標：短讀長測序的偽陽性絕大多數來自基因組比對錯誤，透過嚴格過濾比對品質（Mapping Quality > 56）與片段長度（> 300 bp），演算法 MosaicForecast 在 VAF 約 2% 且深度小於 300 倍時展現出最佳效能；而在結構變異（SV）方面，長讀長測序檢出的數量足足是短讀長的兩倍，特別是插入型變異幾乎只能靠長讀長捕捉，利用 Severus 演算法在約 180 倍 HiFi 深度下能精準偵測低至 0.5%–1% VAF 的微量結構改變；使用個人化組裝（DSA）更使跳躍基因（MEI）在複雜節段重複區的偵測精準度飆升 2.4 倍以上。此外，雙端測序展現出精準量化組織整體突變負荷與組織特異性突變特徵的強大實力，而 PTA 單細胞測序則成功重建了細胞發育譜系樹，並精確捕捉到與抽菸相關的突變印記以及 APOBEC 酵素造成的突變風暴（didyma）。這三大技術相輔相成，正式宣告全基因組體細胞嵌合體分析邁入精準量化時代。
summary.en:
**Summary:** Contrary to the classical textbook view that all somatic cells in an individual share an identical genome, human bodies are complex genetic mosaics. In a benchmark study published in *Cell*, the Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network establishes the first comprehensive, gold-standard roadmap for detecting somatic mutations across the human body. Generating massive multi-platform datasets—exceeding 1,000× short-read and 100–400× long-read sequencing depth across diverse cellular mixtures, clonal models, and normal post-mortem donor tissues—the consortium evaluates the complete spectrum of genetic variations, from single-nucleotide variants to massive structural rearrangements. Their findings demonstrate that integrating personalized diploid assemblies, single-cell amplification, and ultra-accurate duplex sequencing conquers long-standing genomic blind spots, transforming our ability to explore the genetic underpinnings of aging, development, and non-cancer diseases.

**Problem:** Every cell division carries a risk of replication error, generating post-zygotic mutations that accumulate throughout life. While these somatic variations drive tissue aging, cardiovascular anomalies, and neurodevelopmental disorders, identifying them in non-cancerous tissues presents an immense signal-to-noise dilemma. In healthy organs, mosaic mutations often reside in a tiny fraction of cells—yielding variant allele fractions (VAF) far below 5% or even 1%—which conventional 30–50× whole-genome sequencing dismisses as sequencing artifacts. Unlike oncology workflows that contrast hypermutated tumors against matched normal tissues, normal tissue profiling lacks an external baseline. Existing single-cell methods suffer from severe amplification bias and allelic dropout, while standard reference genomes fail in complex repeat-rich regions. The field critically lacked systematic benchmarks and consensus pipelines capable of resolving low-frequency mosaicism genome-wide.

**Approach:** To establish an unassailable truth set, the SMaHT Network engineered four complementary benchmark models: an in vitro mixture of six diverse HapMap cell lines simulating somatic variants across 12 haplotypes at precisely calibrated VAFs (0.25%–16.5%); a 49:1 mixture of melanoma (COLO829) and matched normal lymphoblasts; primary fibroblasts paired with derived clonal iPSC lines capturing natural subclonal evolution; and six post-mortem tissues from four neurotypical donors. These cohorts were interrogated using state-of-the-art sequencing modalities, including deep Illumina short reads, PacBio HiFi, and ultra-long Oxford Nanopore reads. The team rigorously evaluated machine-learning callers, six distinct duplex sequencing platforms, and single-cell primary template-directed amplification (PTA). Crucially, they bypassed standard GRCh38 reference constraints by benchmarking donor-specific diploid assemblies (DSA) and pangenome graph frameworks.

**Results:** The consortium established definitive technical rules for resolving the mosaic genome. False positives for single-nucleotide variants and indels stem primarily from mapping ambiguities; applying stringent filtering thresholds (mapping quality >56, fragment length >300 bp) enabled tools like MosaicForecast to reliably pinpoint variants at ~2% VAF under 300× coverage. For structural variants, long reads discovered roughly twice as many somatic alterations as short reads, with novel insertions being virtually invisible to short-read platforms; callers such as Severus resolved structural variants down to 0.5%–1% VAF at ~180× HiFi coverage. Incorporating donor-specific assemblies boosted mobile element insertion precision by at least 2.4-fold in complex segmental duplications. Finally, the authors revealed a vital triad: while duplex sequencing provides an unbiased readout of tissue-wide mutational burden, and bulk sequencing traces early embryonic lineage expansions, single-cell PTA unmasks cell-private events, APOBEC mutational storms ("didyma"), and immune receptor rearrangements, together enabling high-resolution reconstruction of human developmental lineages.

keyArticle.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of somatic mutation detection by the SMaHT Network
